outline.rationale: The user is new to ML entirely, so the outline builds foundational concepts (neural networks, embeddings, training via gradient descent/backprop) that the confirmed understanding says not to assume. Their goal is reading papers confidently, so the sequence culminates in a node explicitly about decoding paper notation and vocabulary, and every earlier node emphasizes the terminology papers use (tokens, QKV, positional encoding, residuals, encoder/decoder). Attention is split into motivation, mechanics, and multi-head/positional to give conceptual-but-precise depth without collapsing overlap. Implementation/coding and heavy math derivations are excluded per the confirmed scope, so nodes stay at a conceptual level with just enough notation to follow papers. Ordering follows real dependencies: NN basics → representations → attention motivation → attention mechanics → full architecture → training → paper-reading synthesis.
